title: Ivo and the Tide
premise: Beatrix Winterbourne built her wedding-planning empire on the ruins of her own broken engagement, never suspecting that the letter that ended it — a letter she never sent, postmarked eleven years ago — has finally surfaced. When Ivo Marchetti, the man she left without explanation, walks into her office as the brother of her biggest client, old wounds and buried truths collide: he believes she abandoned him for ambition; she believed he chose his family's estate over her. As they plan a wedding neither of them trusts love for, a forged reply and a meddling matriarch's legacy of control come to light, forcing Beatrix to choose between protecting the career that saved her and telling the truth that could destroy it. In the end, she burns the contract, confesses everything at the rehearsal dinner, and meets Ivo at the tide line where they once parted — choosing, this time, the person over the timing.
about_author: Juniper Iversen is a former coastal innkeeper who spent a decade collecting other people's love stories before writing her own down. She lives in a drafty house above a shingle beach, where she writes at dawn and walks the tide line at dusk.

chapters.title: The Letter That Came Late
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. While clearing out her late mother's flat, Beatrix finds an unopened letter addressed to her, postmarked eleven years earlier — in Ivo's handwriting. Her hands shake as she pockets it unread. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in longing; the past knocking politely at the door.

chapters.title: Winterbourne & Co.
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A tour through her flawless wedding-planning empire: immaculate timelines, controlled emotions, a business built on orchestrating joy she no longer believes in. Her assistant notices she hasn't opened the envelope. Emotional beat: polished surface, hollow center.

chapters.title: The Marchetti Booking
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The commission of a lifetime lands: the wedding of Allegra Marchetti at the family's coastal estate. Then Ivo walks into the conference room as estate executor. Eleven years collapse. Emotional beat: shock curdling into defensive professionalism.

chapters.title: What He Remembers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo took this meeting deliberately; he has questions about why Beatrix vanished after his father demanded she leave. He watches her run the meeting like a general and feels both admiration and betrayal. Emotional beat: cold courtesy masking an old, unanswered wound.

chapters.title: Unread
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Alone at night, Beatrix holds the letter over a candle but cannot burn or open it. Flashback fragments: the night she left, the phone call from Ivo's father, the choice she thought she made. Emotional beat: paralysis between knowing and not knowing.

chapters.title: Site Visit
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Walkthrough of the Marchetti estate forces Beatrix and Ivo through the gardens where they once kissed. Bickering over table placements becomes something rawer. Emotional beat: muscle memory of intimacy fighting eleven years of armor.

chapters.title: Allegra's Doubt
chapters.summary: Allegra's POV. The bride privately tells Beatrix she isn't sure she loves her fiancé — only the idea of the family name. Beatrix, who plans weddings she doesn't believe in, gives advice she can't take herself. Emotional beat: complicity in beautiful lies.

chapters.title: The Matriarch's Terms
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Ivo's grandmother, Contessa Vittoria, summons Beatrix: the wedding happens exactly as scripted, or the family withdraws funding from every vendor — including Beatrix's company. She recognizes the same coercion that separated her from Ivo. Emotional beat: recognition and fear.

chapters.title: Storm Shelter
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A storm strands Beatrix and Ivo in the boathouse. Wine loosens history: he accuses her of selling out; she accuses him of choosing the estate. Neither mentions the letter. They almost kiss; she retreats. Emotional beat: anger as the last honest language they share.

chapters.title: Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Beatrix's POV. Full scene of the breakup: the Contessa's ultimatum, the phone call Beatrix made that was never answered, the letter she wrote and mailed anyway. Emotional beat: the reader sees what Beatrix still misremembers.

chapters.title: A Reply That Never Was
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Sorting his late father's papers, Ivo finds a typed 'reply' to Beatrix — cold, dismissive, unsigned by hand. His father's secretary admits the Contessa dictated it. Ivo realizes Beatrix may have written to him and been answered by a forgery. Emotional beat: vertigo; the ground of his grievance shifting.

chapters.title: Opening It
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix finally opens the letter. Ivo's words are tender, urgent, asking her to meet him at the tide line — a meeting she never knew happened because the Contessa intercepted her mail too. Emotional beat: grief for a decade stolen by other people's power.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Estate
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Beatrix confronts Ivo with the letter; he produces the forged reply. For one hour they are twenty-three again — then the Contessa appears, and both retreat behind duty. Emotional beat: truth arriving too fast to hold.

chapters.title: The Career That Saved Everything
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The Contessa offers Beatrix a partnership that would make her firm untouchable — contingent on silence about the letters and on keeping Allegra's doubts out of sight. Beatrix remembers bankruptcy, her mother's debts, everything the career rescued. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a sensible face.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo pressures Allegra gently toward honesty; she accuses him of caring more about Beatrix than her happiness. The Contessa reminds Ivo who controls the estate. He signs the final venue contract with a shaking pen. Emotional beat: loyalty revealed as a cage.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A flawless evening begins to crack: Allegra drinks too much, the fiancé flirts with a guest, the Contessa smiles like a blade. Beatrix watches her own philosophy — beauty over truth — fail in real time. Emotional beat: the mask slipping off everyone at once.

chapters.title: Tide Line
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo waits at the tide line where the letter asked them to meet eleven years ago, half-hoping, half-dreading. Beatrix comes. They speak plainly at last — no accusations, just the whole story laid end to end. Emotional beat: tenderness after wreckage.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Morning of the wedding. Beatrix must decide: sign the partnership and stage another beautiful lie, or tell the truth and lose everything again. She drafts two speeches. Emotional beat: the quiet terror of a decision that cannot be undone.

chapters.title: What Beatrix Said
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. At the reception, Beatrix takes the microphone and instead of a toast, tells the room about two letters, one forgery, and a decade lost to control disguised as love. The Contessa rises; Allegra stands first — and calls off her own wedding. Emotional beat: detonation and strange relief.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Allegra's POV. Fallout: vendors unpaid, the Contessa furious, the industry whispering. But Allegra, freed, thanks Beatrix — and Ivo publicly backs her sister-in-law-to-never-be against the family. Emotional beat: ruin that feels like oxygen.

chapters.title: Rebuilding
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Months later: the firm survives smaller and truer; Beatrix turns down a client whose wedding is a performance, her first honest refusal. Ivo reappears with the original letter framed. Emotional beat: cautious hope, earned rather than granted.

chapters.title: Ivo and the Tide
chapters.summary: Final chapter, alternating POV. On the anniversary of the missed meeting, Ivo proposes nothing grander than showing up — and Beatrix chooses him with open eyes, at last with good timing. They stand where the water erases all footprints and begin again. Emotional beat: second chances, finally kept.
